examples.question_text:
A population satisfies $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=0.003P(1000-P)$.
(a) Write the equation as $kP\left(1-\dfrac{P}{C}\right)$ and identify $k$ and $C$.
(b) Find and interpret the constant solutions.
(c) Explain without calculus when the population grows fastest.

The area $S$ cm$^2$ occupied by a mould satisfies $\dfrac{dS}{dt}=\dfrac{1}{30}S(60-S)$, where $t$ is in days and $S(0)=10$.
Use $\dfrac{1}{S(60-S)}=\dfrac{1}{60}\left(\dfrac{1}{S}+\dfrac{1}{60-S}\right)$ to find $S(t)$.
Find the area after one day, correct to two decimal places, and state the limiting area.
examples.solution_text:
The constant solutions $S=0$ and $S=60$ do not satisfy the initial condition. Invert and use the supplied partial fractions:
$\begin{aligned}\frac{dt}{dS}&=\frac{30}{S(60-S)}\\&=\frac12\left(\frac1S+\frac1{60-S}\right)\end{aligned}$
Integrate and combine the logarithms:
$\begin{aligned}t&=\frac12\left(\ln|S|-\ln|60-S|\right)+D\\\ln\left|\frac{S}{60-S}\right|&=2t-2D\\\frac{S}{60-S}&=Ae^{2t}\end{aligned}$
For $t=0$ and $S=10$, $A=\dfrac{10}{50}=\dfrac15$.
$\begin{aligned}5S&=(60-S)e^{2t}\\S(5+e^{2t})&=60e^{2t}\\S&=\frac{60e^{2t}}{5+e^{2t}}\\&=\frac{60}{1+5e^{-2t}}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}S(1)&=\frac{60}{1+5e^{-2}}\\&\approx35.79\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$
As $t\to\infty$, $e^{-2t}\to0$, so $S\to60$. The limiting area is $60$ cm$^2$.

examples.question_text:
A reserve population satisfies $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=kP\left(1-\dfrac{P}{1800}\right)$, with $P(0)=300$ and $P(3)=600$, where $t$ is in years.
Use $\dfrac{1800}{P(1800-P)}=\dfrac1P+\dfrac1{1800-P}$ to derive $P(t)$ and find $k$ exactly.
Find $P(6)$, the exact time at which $P=1200$, and the exact time at which the population grows fastest.
examples.solution_text:
The equilibria $P=0$ and $P=1800$ do not satisfy $P(0)=300$. Invert and integrate:
$\begin{aligned}\frac{dt}{dP}&=\frac1k\left(\frac1P+\frac1{1800-P}\right)\\t&=\frac1k\left(\ln|P|-\ln|1800-P|\right)+D\\\ln\left|\frac{P}{1800-P}\right|&=kt-kD\\\frac{P}{1800-P}&=Ae^{kt}\end{aligned}$
The initial condition gives $A=\dfrac{300}{1500}=\dfrac15$.
$\begin{aligned}5P&=(1800-P)e^{kt}\\P(5+e^{kt})&=1800e^{kt}\\P&=\frac{1800}{1+5e^{-kt}}\end{aligned}$
Use $P(3)=600$:
$\begin{aligned}600&=\frac{1800}{1+5e^{-3k}}\\1+5e^{-3k}&=3\\e^{-3k}&=\frac25\\k&=\frac13\ln\frac52\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}P(6)&=\frac{1800}{1+5(2/5)^2}\\&=1000\end{aligned}$
For $P=1200$:
$\begin{aligned}1200&=\frac{1800}{1+5e^{-kt}}\\e^{-kt}&=\frac1{10}\\t&=\frac{3\ln10}{\ln(5/2)}\text{ years}\end{aligned}$
Growth is fastest at $P=900$, halfway between the roots of the rate quadratic.
$\begin{aligned}900&=\frac{1800}{1+5e^{-kt}}\\e^{-kt}&=\frac15\\t&=\frac{3\ln5}{\ln(5/2)}\text{ years}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
The proportion $p$ of a community who have heard a message satisfies $\dfrac{dp}{dt}=2p(1-p)$, with $p(0)=\dfrac14$ and $t$ in days.
Use $\dfrac1{p(1-p)}=\dfrac1p+\dfrac1{1-p}$ to find $p(t)$.
Find the percentage who have heard it after one day, to the nearest percent, and the exact time when $75\%$ have heard it.
examples.solution_text:
The constant solutions $p=0$ and $p=1$ do not satisfy the initial condition.
$\begin{aligned}\frac{dt}{dp}&=\frac12\left(\frac1p+\frac1{1-p}\right)\\t&=\frac12\left(\ln|p|-\ln|1-p|\right)+D\\\ln\left|\frac{p}{1-p}\right|&=2t-2D\\\frac{p}{1-p}&=Ae^{2t}\end{aligned}$
At $t=0$, $A=\dfrac{1/4}{3/4}=\dfrac13$.
$\begin{aligned}3p&=(1-p)e^{2t}\\p(3+e^{2t})&=e^{2t}\\p&=\frac1{1+3e^{-2t}}\end{aligned}$
After one day, the percentage is $\dfrac{100}{1+3e^{-2}}\%\approx71\%$.
For $p=\dfrac34$:
$\begin{aligned}\frac34&=\frac1{1+3e^{-2t}}\\1+3e^{-2t}&=\frac43\\e^{-2t}&=\frac19\\t&=\frac12\ln9\\&=\ln3\text{ days}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
(a) A herd satisfies $\dfrac{dH}{dt}=0.2H\left(1-\dfrac{H}{1000}\right)$ with $H(0)=1250$. Without solving the equation, describe its long-term behaviour and justify your answer.
(b) Another population is modelled by $N=\dfrac{2000}{1+7e^{-0.3t}}$. Find its initial and limiting populations. A later count records $2300$ animals; comment on this count in relation to the model.
examples.solution_text:
(a) For $H>1000$, the bracket is negative, so $\dfrac{dH}{dt}<0$. The herd decreases towards $1000$ from above. The equilibrium $H=1000$ cannot be crossed, and is approached without being reached at a finite time.
(b) $\begin{aligned}N(0)&=\frac{2000}{1+7}\\&=250\end{aligned}$
As $t\to\infty$, $e^{-0.3t}\to0$, so $N\to2000$. The initial population is $250$ and the limiting population is $2000$.
Since $7e^{-0.3t}>0$, the model predicts $N<2000$ at every finite time. The count of $2300$ exceeds its carrying capacity, so the model does not describe this count; the assumed capacity is too low for the observed conditions.
